title: PUCSL pushes simple wheeling tariff to unlock private power investment | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 02:12
-     - 6

Director General and CEO Damitha Kumarasinghe — Pic by Ruwan Walpola

By Charumini de Silva

The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) is advocating a simple, transparent, and cost-based wheeling tariff to facilitate private power trading and support investment in energy-intensive sectors, with discussions on the pricing mechanism still at an early stage.

PUCSL Director General and CEO Damitha Kumarasinghe said the tariff should be straightforward to understand, affordable enough to encourage investment, and fair to transmission and distribution companies, covering their costs and providing a reasonable return.

“The wheeling cost should not be exorbitant to discourage investors. It has to be fair to the transmission and distribution companies also,” he said at the Sri Lanka Economic and Investment Summit 2026.

Kumarasinghe said discussions on the tariff had begun but had not progressed significantly, pending the gazetting of relevant legal provisions needed to move the process forward.

PUCSL pushes...

Wheeling allows electricity generated by one party to be transported through the power network for delivery to another customer, subject to applicable charges and regulatory arrangements. It could give businesses greater flexibility in procuring electricity and enable power generators and consumers to enter into supply agreements.

Kumarasinghe said investors should be able to secure power before committing capital to projects, rather than waiting for generation capacity to be developed after an investment decision. Ensuring sufficient electricity is available when businesses are ready to operate is particularly important for attracting new investment, including data centres and other energy-intensive industries.

He said wheeling could allow investors to enter into agreements with power companies to procure electricity in advance, while electricity markets could provide an additional mechanism for balancing supply and demand.

Kumarasinghe estimated that around 15% to 20% of electricity could potentially be traded through a market mechanism, allowing buyers to purchase power to meet their requirements. He said both wheeling and market-based trading options needed to be developed.

When asked about the timeline for wheeling prices, he said it will be finalised soon, but the electricity regulator needs the necessary regulations to go in.

The proposed approach would require a pricing structure that balances the interests of electricity consumers, generators, and network operators without making access to the grid prohibitively expensive.

The comments come amid wider calls from energy-sector stakeholders for regulatory certainty, bankable Power Purchase Agreements, and faster approvals to accelerate investment in renewable generation and related infrastructure.

title: PUCSL approves one-hour daily power cuts for three days amid Lakvijaya outage | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 02:19
-     - 6

The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) has approved one-hour daily power cuts across the country for three consecutive days from 19 to 21 October, if required, to manage electricity demand amid the unavailability of the Lakvijaya Power Station following the blackout on Saturday (17).

The approved demand-management schedules divide the country into four groups, with interruptions staggered across the evening between 4:30 p.m. and 9 p.m. The National System Operator (NSO) CEO Buddhika Samarasinghe announced yesterday that approval had been sought for the temporary power cuts.

Under the schedule for 19 October, Group 1 was allocated an interruption beginning between 4:30 p.m. and 5 p.m., Group 2 between 5:30 p.m. and 6 p.m., Group 3 between 6:30 p.m. and 7 p.m., and Group 4 between 7:30 p.m. and 8 p.m.

For 20 October, the sequence shifts to Group 4, Group 1, Group 2, and Group 3, respectively, across the same staggered time slots. On 21 October, Group 3 will be first, followed by Groups 4, 1, and 2.

Authorities said the interruptions would be implemented only if Electricity Distribution Lanka Ltd., (EDL) needed to manage demand because available generation capacity was insufficient following the Lakvijaya Plant’s unavailability.

Interruption and restoration times may vary by up to 30 minutes, depending on electricity demand, available generation capacity, and prevailing weather conditions.

The three-day schedule provides a temporary demand-management arrangement while the generation shortfall is addressed.

title: LOLC Microfinance Bank Pakistan named ‘Best Turnaround Bank 2026’ | Daily FT

LOLC Microfinance Bank Pakistan, following its remarkable performance over the past two years, has been named ‘Best Turnaround Bank in Pakistan’ in the ‘Medium and Small Tier Category – Banks.’

Pakistan’s banking industry has experienced challenging times over the past several years, with the lingering effects of COVID-19, unprecedented weather conditions, and the country’s economic downturn. 

However, LOLC Microfinance Bank Pakistan has successfully navigated these challenges, demonstrating consistently strong performance across all aspects of its business over the past two years.

The Bank has recorded a Profit After Tax (PAT) of PKR 422.4 million ($ 1.52 million) as at September 2026 and, more importantly, delivered strong business performance across several key indicators:

• Portfolio growth above 204% over the past 12 months

• Growth in public customer deposits of more than 240% over the past 12 months

• Reduction in non-performing loans (NPLs) from 19.5% to less than 2.5% over the past two years.

This achievement is particularly noteworthy within Pakistan’s banking industry, where LOLC Microfinance Bank Pakistan has demonstrated exceptional resilience and one of the strongest turnarounds during this period.

LOLC Group Managing Director Kapila Jayawardena said: “This reflects the strength of the micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) business model, through which we engage with granular and productive segments of the economy where repayment capacity and sustainability are high.” 

He further stated that the bank’s performance across all aspects, including deposit growth, reduction of NPLs, and portfolio growth, reflects its comprehensive performance ahead of the industry.

LOLC Microfinance Bank Pakistan operates through 101 branches, with a total staff of 1,466 and a customer base of 60,000. Marking a major milestone in its growth trajectory, LOLC Microfinance Bank Pakistan has significantly strengthened its operational footprint by relocating its Head Office to Gulberg Greens in Islamabad. Complementing this strategic move, the bank recently expanded its reach with a state-of-the-art branch in Islamabad’s high-profile Blue Area, reflecting its ongoing commitment to enhancing customer access and advancing financial inclusion across key commercial hubs in Pakistan. These infrastructure enhancements position the institution for accelerated market penetration, enabling the seamless delivery of high-impact microfinance solutions to an expanding client base.

title: HSBC service centre to exit Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 02:08
-     - 8

HSBC Electronic Data Processing Lanka Ltd., (HDPL), the bank’s global service centre, will exit Sri Lanka owing to rising costs and an inability to scale.

Staff said they had been notified that they would be let go in four batches as operations relocate to other locations, including India, the Middle East, and the Philippines.

At an all-hands meeting at HDPL’s offices at Mireka Towers in August, staff were told a decision to exit Sri Lanka would be made and communicated in October. On 7 October, they were told they would be let go in four batches, with the first retrenchment in December 2026, followed by batches in May, August, and December 2027.

HDPL had already trimmed staff before this, as various functions were relocated to other service centres.

Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa, meanwhile, warned the move would cost the country 3,000 direct and 500 indirect jobs. In a post on ‘X,’ Premadasa said he had heard that the withdrawal was scheduled to be completed in December 2027.

“It would spell a significant economic setback for our motherland,” he said.

HDPL began operations in April 2004 and supports customers across 24 markets in North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. Its work includes fund administration, banking transaction processing, customer due diligence, financial crime risk screening, and trade transactions.

Earlier this year, HSBC exited the retail banking business in Sri Lanka.

title: Microfinance lenders to  accept public deposits mooted | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 02:06
-     - 5

MP Lakmali Hemachandra

Proposals to allow existing microfinance institutions to accept limited public deposits under regulatory supervision, simplify their licensing process, and facilitate access to lower-cost funding were put forward at a meeting of a Parliamentary committee, as the panel focused on expediting implementation of the Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Act.

Microfinance...

The Sectoral Oversight Committee on Economic Development and International Relations, chaired by MP Lakmali Hemachandra, met recently at Parliament with officials of the Lanka Microfinance Practitioners’ Association, the Parliament Secretariat said yesterday.

The proposals emerged as discussions covered the licensing process for institutions engaged in microfinance activities, legal and practical challenges relating to certain provisions of the Act, restrictions on accepting deposits, and the cost of funds.

Attention was also drawn to the possibility of reducing lending interest rates by establishing a mechanism to channel concessional funding from international institutions, such as the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to regulated microfinance institutions. Concessional funding is lending at below-market interest rates, typically from multilateral lenders.

The meeting emphasised the need to expedite implementation of the Act, which was enacted to regulate the microfinance and lending sectors. It highlighted the importance of controlling lending institutions that impose excessively high interest rates through informal practices and cause hardship to the public, alongside the need to establish a fair regulatory environment for properly functioning microfinance institutions.

The implementation of the Act’s consumer protection provisions, the time required to establish the Regulatory Authority, and the deadlines granted to institutions to obtain licences were also discussed.

The meeting was attended by MPs Lakshman Nipuna Arachchi, Sagarika Athauda, Kanthasamy Prabhu, Thilina Samarakoon, Wijesiri Basnayake, Suranga Rathnayake, and Sivagnanam Sritharan, along with officials from the Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Ministry.

title: SLPA to develop new logistics hub at Port of Colombo after earlier JV scrapped | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 02:05
-     - 11

The Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) yesterday said it has decided to pursue the development of a new logistics hub within Port of Colombo through a public-private partnership (PPP) following the decision of the shareholders not to proceed with the previously proposed joint venture (JV) involving China Merchants Port Holdings Company Ltd., through its fully owned subsidiary and Access Engineering PLC.

The earlier project was intended to establish a modern logistics facility within Port of Colombo through a JV company known as South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub (SACLH).

The company was established in 2023 with the participation of three shareholders: China Merchants Port Holdings Company Ltd., through its fully owned subsidiary holding a 70% equity stake, and the SPLA and Access Engineering PLC, each holding a 15% equity stake.

The proposed project envisaged a total investment of approximately $ 280 million, with a planned floor capacity of approximately 150,000 square metres. The initiative was originally conceived to enhance the logistics capabilities of Port of Colombo and strengthen its position as a major regional maritime and logistics centre.

However, following an assessment of the prevailing external circumstances, commercial considerations, and the interests of the respective shareholders, a decision was reached not to proceed with the proposed JV.

Under the agreed arrangements, the three shareholders will receive refunds of their respective equity contributions, subject to applicable regulatory requirements and operational expenses. The total amount to be refunded is approximately $ 29.8 million, which will be distributed among the shareholders in proportion to their respective equity contributions by SACLH.

Notwithstanding the decision to discontinue the earlier JV, the SLPA remains committed to developing modern logistics infrastructure within Port of Colombo to meet the evolving requirements of international maritime trade and supply chains.

Accordingly, the SLPA has decided to pursue an alternative development strategy through the establishment of a new logistics hub under a PPP model, through a competitive bidding process with relevant approvals.

The proposed development will utilise a substantial land area within Port of Colombo to establish a modern, integrated logistics facility capable of supporting a wide range of port-related and value-added logistics activities.

The initiative is expected to facilitate the transformation of Port of Colombo from a predominantly container transshipment hub into a comprehensive maritime and logistics hub, providing enhanced services to shipping lines, cargo owners, logistics operators, and other stakeholders in the international supply chain.

The proposed PPP approach is also expected to create opportunities for private-sector participation, attract investment, optimise the utilisation of valuable port land and infrastructure, and generate sustainable long-term revenue for the SLPA.

The development of an integrated logistics hub is considered an important component of the SLPA’s broader strategy to strengthen the competitiveness of Port of Colombo, improve operational efficiency, and expand its role in regional and international trade.

The SLPA emphasises that the decision not to proceed with the earlier JV does not represent a departure from its commitment to logistics infrastructure development. Rather, it provides an opportunity to pursue an alternative development model that better aligns with the Authority’s strategic priorities, commercial objectives, and the long-term interests of Port of Colombo.

The SLPA said it remains firmly committed to positioning Port of Colombo as a leading maritime, transshipment, and logistics hub in South Asia, while ensuring that future port development initiatives are commercially viable, financially sustainable, and aligned with Sri Lanka’s national economic interests.

title: State company seeks exclusive mining rights | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 02:05
-     - 11

State-owned Lanka Mineral Sands asks that northeastern coastline deposits not be allocated to other private institutions, seeks mining rights for 68 grids

A Parliamentary committee has decided to issue the necessary recommendations on matters relating to the granting of mining rights for 68 grids to State-owned Lanka Mineral Sands Ltd., (LMSL). The company has sought exclusive mining rights over mineral sand deposits along the northeastern coastline.

LMSL submitted a request to the Sectoral Oversight Committee on Economic Development and International Relations seeking these exclusive rights, and asked that the deposits not be allocated to other private institutions, the Parliament Secretariat said yesterday.

State...

 The Committee, chaired by MP Lakmali Hemachandra, also considered the provision of operational support to the company.

The review of mineral mining licences issued in the past, the necessary action to be taken regarding irregular licences, and the transfer of the relevant mineral deposits to LMSL were also discussed. It was noted that steps had been taken to forward information concerning certain irregularities identified in the recent past to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).

Discussions focused on ensuring a long-term and uninterrupted supply of raw materials for value-added industries by utilising mineral sand deposits along the eastern coastline. In line with the Government’s policy of exporting mineral sands as value-added products rather than merely as raw materials, the Committee also considered implementing value-addition projects by attracting both local and foreign investors.

Attention was also drawn to implementing a multi-agency committee mechanism to ensure transparency and coordination among relevant institutions when issuing mineral mining licences in the future.

The Committee’s deliberations follow the Government’s push to turn Sri Lanka into a mineral processing hub. Addressing the Mineral Sands Technical Conference in June, Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Minister Sunil Handunnetti said the Government’s new National Mineral Policy was aimed at transforming Sri Lanka from a supplier of raw mineral resources into a competitive mineral processing hub (https://www.ft.lk/top-story/Global-experts-map-path-to-unlock-Sri-Lanka-s-mineral-wealth/26-793436).

Industry assessments presented at the Conference indicated the country possesses around 604 million tonnes of mineral sands, although experts noted that the resource potential remains underexplored in the absence of a comprehensive islandwide geophysical survey. Sri Lanka’s mineral export potential is estimated at $ 778 million under the International Trade Centre’s Export Potential Map, while a Pathfinder Foundation report estimated the longer-term opportunity could approach $ 2 billion if downstream processing, value addition, and mineral-based manufacturing are developed.

Speaking at the same forum, Australian High Commissioner Matthew Duckworth cautioned that attracting long-term investment into the sector would require transparent regulation, predictable approval processes, policy consistency, and strong environmental governance.

The private sector has warned that policy ambition alone will not unlock investment. The Chamber of Mineral Exporters (CME), representing exporters and explorers of quartz, graphite, mineral sands, and mica, has described the National Mineral Policy as a welcome first step.

However, it argued that the real test lies in how the Geological Survey and Mines Bureau (GSMB) and the Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Ministry implement it through regulations, licensing reforms, and institutional change.

The Chamber cited previous mineral allocation exercises in which companies with established processing facilities and export operations lost access to deposits to proposals promising sophisticated downstream manufacturing that ultimately failed to materialise. It argued that such experiences have weakened confidence in the credibility of regulatory decision-making.

The CME also raised concern over licensing uncertainty. It said exploration and mining companies have invested millions of dollars, recruited staff, and completed geological work only to find projects effectively frozen while the Government finalises new procedures. It warned that prolonged regulatory pauses risk damaging Sri Lanka’s reputation among international investors, particularly when companies have already committed capital in good faith.

The Chamber argued that the State should focus on creating a stable regulatory environment rather than attempting to direct commercial outcomes. In its view, the Government’s role is to establish clear rules, uphold environmental standards, and provide investment and policy certainty, while allowing businesses to determine where commercially viable value addition can occur (https://www.ft.lk/top-story/Mineral-exporters-urge-GSMB-reforms-to-unlock-investment-potential/26-794883).

The meeting was attended by MPs Lakshman Nipuna Arachchi, Sagarika Athauda, Kanthasamy Prabhu, Thilina Samarakoon, Wijesiri Basnayake, Suranga Rathnayake, and Sivagnanam Sritharan, along with officials from the Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Ministry.

title: Customs seizes  Rs. 67.5 m in drugs  from foreign mail parcels | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 02:04
-     - 10

Sri Lanka Customs has seized narcotics worth an estimated Rs. 67.5 million from 11 foreign postal parcels at the Central Mail Exchange in Colombo.

The parcels, sent from eight countries, contained more than 3.1 kilograms of Kush cannabis, 2,395 grams of MDMA (Ecstasy) pills, and 33 grams of Mandy, a crystal or powder form of MDMA.

Customs said officers of its Narcotics Control Unit (NCU) identified the parcels over the past few months during routine inspections of incoming international mail. The parcels were detained pending collection, and when the recipients failed to collect them within the stipulated period, NCU officers examined them yesterday together with the Police Narcotic Bureau (PNB).

The cannabis, valued at over Rs. 30.5 million, came from Thailand, the US, and the UK. The MDMA pills were sent from Belgium, France, Canada, and Germany, and the Mandy from the Netherlands.

The largest single detection was a parcel from Belgium containing 2,202 grams of MDMA pills valued at an estimated Rs. 33 million.

The narcotics have been handed over to the PNB for further investigation and legal proceedings.

title: 11th Dialog Club Vision Rotary Par 3 Golf Classic: Celebrating decade of golfing for a cause | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 01:27
-     - 5

The 11th Dialog Club Vision Rotary Par 3 Golf Classic, organised by the Rotary Club of Colombo Metropolitan (RCCM) in partnership with title sponsor Dialog Club Vision, will take place at the Royal Colombo Golf Club (RCGC) on Saturday, 24 October 2026. 

What sets the Rotary Par 3 Golf Classic apart is its distinctive tournament format: the Club’s traditional 18-hole course is transformed into a par-54 layout, with every hole played as a par 3. This unique format challenges golfers to demonstrate precision, distance control and skill around the greens, while offering an exciting opportunity for a birdie or even a hole-in-one on every hole. The tournament has become a much-anticipated fixture on the golfing calendar, combining competitive play with the chance to support meaningful charitable causes. Players will compete in two sessions, teeing off at 7:00 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.

Over the years, the Rotary Par 3 Golf Classic has grown into one of RCCM’s flagship fundraising initiatives, supporting projects that extend beyond the golf course and make a tangible difference in communities across Sri Lanka. Through its charitable activities, RCCM has supported paediatric heart surgeries, critical medical equipment for hospitals, programs for children with disabilities, educational initiatives and community welfare projects. 

Commenting on the club’s positive impact, Rotary Club of Colombo Metropolitan President Joevinie Machado said: “As we celebrate the eleventh edition of the Rotary Par 3 Classic, we are reminded that this tournament is about much more than golf. It represents what can be achieved when individuals, businesses and communities come together with a shared commitment to making a difference. The funds raised have helped us support life-saving healthcare for children and sustain several other community projects. We are deeply grateful to Dialog Club Vision, the Royal Colombo Golf Club, our corporate partners and the golfers who have continued to support this initiative. Their generosity enables us to turn a day of sporting camaraderie into meaningful and lasting change.”

Children’s healthcare remains a central focus of RCCM’s charitable work. Among its recent initiatives, the Club has supported the purchase of a paediatric ultrasound scanner valued at Rs. 3.5 million for the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University Hospital and the donation of a portable, reusable video laryngoscope to Lady Ridgeway Hospital to assist medical teams in managing paediatric airways. The club has also supported improvements to critical care facilities at Lady Ridgeway Hospital through a Rs. 27.6 million contribution towards advanced patient monitoring equipment, transport modules, capnography equipment and specialised accessories for intensive care and high-dependency units. These investments are intended to strengthen the hospital’s capacity to monitor and care for critically ill infants and children.

Royal Colombo Golf Club Captain Mahela Jayawardena, Bank of Ceylon Chief Marketing Officer Sameera Liyanage, Rotary Club of Colombo Metropolitan President Joevinie Machado and Project Chair Suresh Ganeshan

Through its Two Hearts Children’s Heart Surgery Project, RCCM is also working to improve access to life-saving cardiac surgery for underprivileged children diagnosed with atrial and ventricular septal defects. The initiative, with Rs. 15 million in funding support, aims to reduce waiting times by facilitating surgeries at selected private hospitals, in coordination with the relevant healthcare authorities.

Beyond healthcare, RCCM continues to support a range of community initiatives, including its annual Sunshine Games for children with disabilities, educational assistance and feeding programmes for vulnerable children. These projects reflect the Club’s broader commitment to creating opportunities and improving the well-being of underserved communities.

Dialog Axiata Chief of Group Customer Experience Ayomal Gunasekera said the tournament’s run demonstrates the wider power of sport: “Dialog Club Vision is proud to support both the Rotary Club of Colombo Metropolitan and the Rotary Par 3 Golf Classic as it marks its 11th edition. Having supported this initiative over the past nine years, and as title sponsor for the second consecutive year, we have witnessed the lasting impact that strong partnerships can create for communities across Sri Lanka. What makes this tournament truly special is that it brings together organisations and individuals around a shared purpose, transforming a sporting event into a platform for meaningful social impact. We are pleased to continue supporting efforts that expand access to healthcare and help create brighter futures for children and families.”

Asia Securities, is the Platinum Sponsor of the event. Commenting on this year’s sponsorship, which marks the sixth consecutive year of partnership with RCCM for the tournament, Asia Securities Executive Director Avancka Herat said, “We are pleased to continue our partnership with the Rotary Par 3 Classic 2026. We keep coming back to support this event as its contribution to the ‘Rotary for Little Hearts’ initiative closely aligns with Asia Securities’ vision of creating impact beyond our boundaries, and sharing our success with the broader community.” Asia Securities offers wealth management, equities, and investment banking services to a broad spectrum of institutional, high-net-worth, and retail clients. The firm has consistently been recognised as Sri Lanka’s #1 stockbroker for the 4th consecutive year.   

As a key partner in the tournament’s ongoing success, the Royal Colombo Golf Club provides the setting for this annual sporting and fundraising initiative. Speaking on the occasion, Royal Colombo Golf Club Captain Mahela Jayawardena said: “The RCGC is honoured to partner with the RCCM for the eleventh consecutive year. Beyond driving impactful community work island-wide, the club is deeply committed to local outreach and uplifting the families within our extended staff and community, including providing school books for their children.”

Royal Colombo Golf Club Captain Mahela Jayawardena, Asia Securities Executive Director Avancka Herat, Rotary Club of Colombo Metropolitan President Joevinie Machado and Project Chair Suresh Ganeshan

Gold Partner Bank of Ceylon, supporting the tournament for the second year, reaffirmed its commitment to the community. Sameera Liyanage, Chief Marketing Officer of Bank of Ceylon, said: “As the economic driver of Sri Lanka, Bank of Ceylon believes our responsibility extends beyond banking. Through our ‘Beyond Banking’ commitment, we support initiatives in healthcare, education, sports and culture that enrich lives and strengthen communities. Our partnership with the Dialog Club Vision Rotary Par 3 Golf Classic reflects this commitment, particularly in supporting children’s healthcare and access to life-saving treatment. We believe investing in the health and well-being of our children is an investment in the future of our nation.”

The tournament is also supported by Technomedics, AppiGo and Würth, whose contributions, together with those of the principal partners and participating golfers, help sustain this annual fundraising initiative. As the Rotary Par 3 Golf Classic marks its eleventh edition, RCCM looks forward to building on the tournament’s legacy, strengthening its partnerships and continuing to channel the spirit of sport into meaningful support for children and communities across Sri Lanka.

title: Remembering Thajone Savanghan and the great Havelocks team of 1976 | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 01:26
-     - 4

Thajone Savanghan chaired by the jubilant Havelocks team after winning the Clifford Cup in 1976

By Frankie Hubert 

This October marks 50 years since the all-conquering Havelocks, led by the incomparable Thajone Savanghan, captured the blue riband of Sri Lankan rugby — the Clifford Cup.

For me, this anniversary is also an opportunity to remember and celebrate a remarkable man who encouraged me, inspired me and, above all, became a very dear friend.

When the great tales of Sri Lankan rugby are told, Thajone stands tall among the finest. In a country where rugby union has always held a special place, his exploits deserve to be revisited as we celebrate the 50th anniversary of that magnificent Havelocks team — the side that won the rare double of the league championship and Clifford Cup under his brilliant leadership.

I joined the Havies in 1975 while I was still at St Peter’s College. I played against S. Thomas’ on a Friday and, incredibly, played my first club match for Havelocks the very next day against the Air Force. We won both games.

By then, Thajone was already a legend. As a wing forward, he was renowned for his bone-crushing tackles — tackles that many of us would come to feel throughout our own careers. The famous sports writer TMK Samat aptly described him as “the boy with the 10-ton tackle.” 

Thajone and his elder brother, Jurangan, were among the outstanding players who helped spark the renaissance of rugby at Isipathana College in the late 1960s. Thajone went on to skipper a Colombo XV against the mighty Bosuns from the UK.

When I first met Thajone, I was in awe of his ability to read the game. He seemed to see things developing before the rest of us had even realised they were happening.

In 1976, Thajone was appointed captain, and he immediately set the perfect example. Knowing that leadership demanded sacrifice, he gave up alcohol for the entire season — no small undertaking for someone who was known to enjoy a drink! That gesture earned the immediate respect of his teammates.

Thajone led from the front. He demanded discipline at practice and on match days, and he expected everyone to give their best for the jersey. Yet, despite his seriousness about rugby, he also had an extraordinary ability to lighten the mood.

His quick wit and mischievous smile were infectious. He could tell a completely believable story with the straightest of faces, leaving us hanging on every word, only for the punchline to reveal the joke and have the entire room in stitches. To this day, I have never met anyone quite like Thajone when it came to telling stories and jokes, and then completely cracking up himself as he delivered the punchline.

On the pitch, he was a superb leader.

I believe we won every match in  1976, capturing the Clifford Cup — the jewel in the crown of Sri Lankan rugby at the time — as well as the Knockout Cup, if memory serves me correctly, beating Navy 15–3 in the final at Longden Place.

But one match stands out above all others.

We travelled to Nittawela to play Kandy SC knowing that we had to win by 25 points to clinch the league title. On paper, it seemed almost impossible.

Kandy, playing on their home ground, were among the fiercest opponents in the country. Add a muddy pitch and some of the most passionate and boisterous supporters in Sri Lanka, and you can imagine the noise and hostility when we ran onto the field. Yet, despite the conditions and the atmosphere, we were quietly confident that we could do the impossible.

Before the match, Thajone gave us one of his typically brief but powerful team talks. He reminded us that every player was there on merit and that each of us had a responsibility to give everything for the team.

Then, almost immediately, the drama began. In the very first minute, I kicked a high up-and-under towards their fullback and chased it down, only to be decked by a punch from their wing forward, Viper Gunaratne Jr. I was left lying on the ground, bleeding.

Thajone rushed over to me, tears in his eyes, and told the referee, Colonel CS Fernando:

“Sir, Frankie’s career is over!”

The referee immediately sent Gunaratne off, sending shockwaves through the home crowd.

As it happened, his elder brother, Viper Gunaratne Sr., had also felled me in my very first game against the Sri Lanka Air Force!

Then Thajone looked at me, gave me that familiar wink and said:

“OK, now get up and play, Frankie!”

And play is exactly what we did. We went on to win 28–0 and secured the league crown.

What a man. What a captain.

The great Havies team of 1976 included: Thajone Savanghan (Captain/flanker);  Jeyer Rodriguesz;  Riztharin Morseth (hooker); Gavin Stevens; Stefan De Silva;; Royden de Silva; Anton Benedict (future 1978 captain); Jeffrey de Jong (future 1977 captain); Jeffrey Yu (future 1979 captain); Lanil Tennakoon; Hanzil Samad (Scrum-half); Frank Hubert (future captain 1980); Hazari Hameed; Hafi Abdeen; Chula Warusavitarne; David Nicolle;  PL Moonasinghe; Marco de Silva;  Coach: Dicky Jayatilleke.

Thajone retired in 1977, choosing to step aside to give younger players an opportunity. We missed him enormously, but his example remained with us. Many of us went on to continue the winning tradition at the Havies, inspired by the standards he had set.

The great forward Anton Benedict, who captained both Police and Havelocks to championships, remembers Thajone as the consummate professional on the field and recalled the unique character of that team.

“The 1976 squad was a happy blend of talented schoolboy ruggerites in their teens who had their initial exposure to club rugby as well as those who had loads of experience,” Benedict recalled.

“Thajone, our Captain Cool, led by example. If my memory serves me well, it was the first-ever Havies team rewarded with a couple of matches in Singapore. The architect of the travel arrangements by sea on board the passenger ship, Chidambaram, was the amiable and respected coach Nimal Maralande. May his soul rest in peace.”

Benna later skippered the Havies to the grand triple in 1978. Those memories capture something special about that era — the camaraderie, the characters and the friendships that made club rugby so much more than what happened on the field.

Our paths crossed less frequently after Thajone’s playing career, but in the mid-1980s our friendship was rekindled when I was living in Oman, and he was in Dubai. We shared many wonderful times over the years, enjoying great gatherings, laughter and friendship. Whenever I travelled to Dubai for the prestigious Dubai Rugby Sevens, I would often stay at Thajone’s home. Those were special times, and the memories remain incredibly precious to me.

I am writing this because I want to make sure the legend of Thajone — and the great Havelocks team of 1976 — is never forgotten. Thajone was dynamic and charismatic, both on and off the rugby field. He was a fierce competitor, a natural leader, a wonderful storyteller and, above all, a great friend.

And whenever we met, there was one song we would always sing together: “For the Good Times.”

Looking back now, I realise just how fortunate and blessed I was to have been not only his teammate, but also his close friend. The world lost a truly amazing man when Thajone passed away in September 2009.

To Noorani, his beloved wife, to his sons Dilshan and Romesh, and to their families, I send my love and deepest affection.

Thajone, thank you for the memories, the laughter, the lessons and the friendship. You will always be remembered.

(The author played for Havelocks 1975–1981)

title: Mohamed Safran wins long jump bronze for Sri Lanka  at Asian Para Games | Daily FT

By Hishan Welmilla

Sri Lanka’s Mohamed Safran secured a bronze medal in the men’s long jump T47 event at the 5th Asian Para Games, producing an impressive final attempt to finish on the podium.

Safran leapt 6.55 metres in his final attempt to claim third place, delivering a crucial performance when it mattered most. His effort also pushed his teammate Yusuf Salman out of medal contention after Salman had been in a strong position heading into the final round.

Salman, who had recorded a jump of 6.40 metres, was placed third before the final attempts. However, he could manage only 6.28 metres in his last jump, which was not enough to retain his podium position. As a result, Salman finished fourth, narrowly missing out on a medal in a closely contested competition between the two Sri Lankan athletes.

India’s Nishad Kumar claimed the gold medal with an outstanding jump of 7.11 metres, while Uzbekistan’s Omadbek Khasanov secured the silver medal with a distance of 6.99 metres.

Safran’s bronze medal added another achievement to Sri Lanka’s campaign at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, highlighting the country’s growing competitiveness in para athletics.

Although Salman narrowly missed the podium, his performance demonstrated Sri Lanka’s strength in the event, with two athletes challenging for medals against some of Asia’s leading long jumpers.

Safran’s decisive final jump proved to be the defining moment of the competition for Sri Lanka, ensuring the national flag was represented on the medal podium.

title: Britain’s Kartal misses out on biggest title of her career | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 01:23
-     - 3

Sonay Kartal

Britain’s Sonay Kartal missed out on what would have been the biggest title of her career as she faded in a gripping Wuhan Open final against French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

Kartal, 24, was bidding to lift the trophy in only her third event since returning from a six-month absence caused by a back injury.

But an extraordinary week in China seemed to catch up with Kartal as she ran out of steam - physically and mentally - in a 2-6 6-4 6-2 defeat.

Kartal was playing in just the 10th match of her impressive comeback and was attempting to become the first Briton to win a WTA 1,000 title since Johanna Konta in 2017.

Ranked 170th in the world at the start of the event, Kartal reached Sunday’s final by seeing off a host of notable opponents, including current top-10 players and former major champions.

However, Poland’s Chwalinska, who made a shock run to this year’s Roland Garros final, dragged Kartal into a brutal battle and ultimately got the better of it.

Kartal dominated the first set and led by a break in the second before Chwalinska turned momentum in her favour.

Chwalinska, 25, felt a few nerves as she closed in on her first WTA 1,000 title, but took her third championship point when Kartal hammered a forehand long.

Despite losing the final, Kartal has enjoyed a transformational week which even she did not see coming.

On Monday, she will climb back into the world’s top 50 - just below her career high - and become the British number one for the first time. She also earned prize money of about £290,000.

title: Rivalries return: Ceylon Golf League set for January 2027 | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 01:22
-     - 7

The Ceylon Golf League (CGL), Sri Lanka’s first franchise-based golf league, will return for its second season from 8–10 January 2027, at the Royal Colombo Golf Club (RCGC), with Nations Trust Bank joining as Title Partner and over 150 players registered ahead of the upcoming player auction.

Season 2 will feature eight city-based franchises competing for the title, with reigning champions Nuwara Eliya Panthers set to defend their crown. Last season’s runners-up, Trinco Sharks, will lead the challenge alongside the other franchises seeking to claim the championship.

The announcement was made at the league’s Season 2 press conference at Cheers Pub, Cinnamon Grand. The inaugural season attracted 130 players and more than 2,600 attendees, introducing a franchise-based team format to Sri Lankan golf through a player auction, city rivalries and three days of competition.

With over 150 players registered and 35 players released across the eight franchises, teams will have an opportunity to restructure their squads at the Player Auction scheduled for 23 October at The Atrium, Cinnamon Grand.

Ceylon Golf League Co-Founder Shamal Perera said: “The first season showed us how much appetite there is for franchise golf in Sri Lanka. Players embraced the team competition, the rivalries came alive, and we now have a foundation to build on.” 

 “Together with my partners Mahela Jayawardena and Suhayb Sangani, we’re excited to bring CGL back for its second season. Having Nations Trust Bank join us as Title Partner, alongside our other partners, gives us real momentum as we look ahead to the auction and another competitive three days at the RCGC,” he added.

The three-day competition will open with Foursomes on 8 January, followed by Fourball on 9 January, before concluding with Indies in a one-versus-three format on 10 January. Teams will compete across seven handicap categories covering male and female divisions.

With the player auction approaching and the defending champions preparing to return, the second season is set to build on the inaugural tournament’s participation and audience, as the eight franchises compete for the Ceylon Golf League title.

Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two strokes to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy.

Spain’s Chacarra finished on 21 under, with American Reed and world number two McIlroy well off the pace by the final round of this event.

After opening with successive scores of 67 in his first two rounds at Delhi Golf Club, bad light halted play with Chacarra still on the 11th hole of his third round on Saturday.

That left the 26-year-old with extra work on Sunday and he concluded his third round with a five-shot lead after a nine-under 63.

A two-under 70 in his final round was then enough to see off the challenge of New Zealand’s Daniel Hillier who birdied the last to put the pressure on the victor.

The win was Chacarra’s third of the season as he looks to emulate Jon Rahm and Seve Ballesteros to become the third Spaniard to top the season-long standings on the DP World Tour.

title: ICC fines Sri Lanka, Pakistan for slow over-rates | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 01:16
-     - 5

Sri Lanka Captain Kusal Mendis, Pakistan Captain Shaheen Shah Afridi

The International Cricket Council (ICC) has fined Sri Lanka and Pakistan for slow over-rates in the opening match of the One Day International (ODI) Tri-Series in Rawalpindi on 18 October, 2026.

Sri Lanka were fined 5% of their match fees for finishing one over short of the required target, while Pakistan were fined 10% for falling two overs short, after time allowances were taken into consideration, the ICC said.

Under the ICC Code of Conduct, players are fined 5% of their match fees for every over their team fails to bowl within the allotted time.

ICC Elite Panel Match Referee Jeff Crowe imposed the sanctions. Sri Lanka Captain Kusal Mendis and Pakistan Captain Shaheen Shah Afridi pleaded guilty and accepted the penalties, avoiding the need for formal hearings.

The charges were levelled by on-field umpires Asif Yaqoob and Wayne Knights, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Faisal Afridi.

Browns Hotels and Resorts has secured five prestigious accolades at the South Asian Travel Awards (SATA) 2026, held in the Maldives, earning two Gold and three Silver awards across five properties in its portfolio.

Leading the Gold wins, Newburgh Ella – The Tea Factory Resort clinched South Asia’s Best New Hotel, while Ayugiri Ayurveda Wellness Resort secured South Asia’s Leading Wellness Resort.

As the newest addition to the Browns Hotels and Resorts portfolio, Newburgh Ella – The Tea Factory Resort, under the leadership of General Manager Gangadara Velasamy, is a former tea factory dating back to 1903, transformed into a contemporary hospitality experience. This significant achievement, places the property among the region’s leading new hospitality offerings and recognises its unique identity in a competitive field of hotels from across Asia.

Its historic architecture and considered design preserve the character of the original factory while introducing modern comforts. The tea factory tour and immersive tea experiences set Newburgh Ella apart as a one-of-a-kind experience in Asia. The property also operates as a fully paperless hotel, embracing digital solutions across its operations to enhance efficiency and support more sustainable hospitality practices.

The experience extends beyond the property into the surrounding landscapes of Ella, with access to renowned attractions and trails, including Ella Rock, Little Adam’s Peak and the Pekoe Trail.

Winning Gold at the South Asian Travel Awards 2026 as South Asia’s Leading Wellness Resort, Ayugiri Ayurveda Wellness Resort in Sigiriya, led by General Manager Sujeewa de Zoysa, offers a considered approach to luxury wellness. Set across 44 acres in Sigiriya, the resort combines personalised wellbeing with Sri Lanka’s rich cultural heritage and abundant wildlife, including opportunities for elephant spotting.

Guided by its philosophy, The Art of Living Well, Ayugiri features 22 suites with private plunge pools, including two Presidential Suites. Its wellness experiences include personalised programmes, yoga, meditation, sound healing and treatments at the Ayuwasa Wellness Centre, complemented by the Beheth Oruwa, a traditional medicinal boat, and a resident doctor-led approach to wellbeing.

The experience extends to dining, with international gourmet cuisine and authentic local flavours served in memorable settings, from lakeside locations to a rock-top setting, tree hut and a restaurant with the view of the Sigiriya rock.

At Club Hotel Dolphin in Negombo, General Manager Manoj Perera and his team clinched South Asia’s Leading All-Inclusive Resort for the third consecutive time, reinforcing the property’s established reputation for energetic, experience-led family holidays, with an extensive range of dining, leisure and entertainment activities for guests of all ages.

Cluster General Manager Rohan Gamage and the team at The Eden Beruwala secured the Silver award for South Asia’s Leading Beach Resort for the second consecutive time. Located along Sri Lanka’s renowned Golden Mile, this five-star beachfront resort combines coastal surroundings with varied dining experiences, including beach dining, alongside a range of watersports and leisure activities.

Lantern Boutique Hotel by Reveal the Collection, part of Browns Hotels and Resorts, clinched the Silver award for South Asia’s Leading Boutique Hotel, celebrating its approach to boutique hospitality. Led by General Manager Sharmen Perera, the property is located in Mirissa and offers an intimate, design-led stay shaped by its coastal surroundings.

Browns Hotels and Resorts Director/Chief Executive Officer Eksath Wijeratne said: “What makes this achievement particularly meaningful for Browns Hotels and Resorts is the diversity of the recognition. Each property has its own identity, purpose and guest proposition, yet all share the same commitment to delivering memorable and elevated experiences and showcasing the best of Sri Lankan hospitality. These accolades belong to the people behind every guest experience, whose dedication and passion make the difference every day. We look forward to welcoming more travellers to discover our properties, experience Sri Lanka in different ways and create stories of their own.”

title: USA - Sri Lanka Chamber of Commerce plans New York campaign to promote Sri Lankan tourism and businesses | Daily FT

The USA–Sri Lanka Chamber of Commerce is exploring an innovative promotional initiative to showcase Sri Lanka’s tourism, cultural heritage and business opportunities in the heart of New York City during the upcoming Christmas and holiday season. 

The proposed campaign aims to bring Sri Lanka’s unique identity to one of the world’s most internationally recognised cities through a mobile digital billboard featuring high-quality photographs and videos highlighting the island’s natural beauty, rich heritage and diverse commercial offerings. 

The initiative is designed to capitalise on New York City’s significant holiday-season foot traffic, reaching American consumers, international tourists and potential business partners.

The digital showcase would feature Sri Lanka’s pristine beaches, scenic mountains, waterfalls, tea plantations, wildlife, ancient cities, Buddhist heritage, traditional arts, authentic cuisine and modern attractions, positioning the country as an attractive international travel destination. A QR code linking to tourism information could also be incorporated, allowing interested viewers to explore Sri Lanka’s attractions and travel opportunities. Beyond destination promotion, the proposed initiative seeks to provide Sri Lankan businesses with a platform to introduce their products and services to the American market. 

Businesses representing Ceylon tea, spices, food products, gems and jewellery, apparel, handicrafts, wellness, hospitality and tourism, among other sectors, would have the opportunity to showcase their brands alongside the broader national promotional campaign. The initiative could be particularly beneficial to small and medium-sized Sri Lankan enterprises seeking greater international exposure, brand recognition and potential commercial partnerships in the US. 

By integrating tourism promotion with commercial visibility, the Chamber aims to strengthen Sri Lanka’s international image while supporting opportunities for trade, investment and business development. The proposed campaign also seeks to encourage collaboration among Sri Lankan businesses, tourism stakeholders and other organisations interested in promoting the country internationally. Under the central message of “Discover Sri Lanka. Experience Sri Lanka. Visit Sri Lanka,” the campaign would present the island as a destination offering natural beauty, cultural richness, distinctive products and entrepreneurial potential. 

Through this initiative, the USA–Sri Lanka Chamber of Commerce hopes to create a collective promotional platform that brings Sri Lanka closer to international audiences while opening new opportunities for Sri Lankan tourism and businesses in the US. For more information, visit www.usaslcc.org.

Ashane began his career as a Front Office Trainee at Cinnamon Red Colombo, gaining an understanding of guest service before moving into sales. His final position with the group was Senior Manager – Sales at Cinnamon Bentota Beach, where he contributed to the resort’s transition into Cinnamon’s luxury Signature Selection.

This breadth gives couples, families and groups the freedom to combine relaxation, discovery and shared experiences within one Kalutara setting.

title: Heritance Hotels and Resorts secures 4 wins at World Travel Awards 2026 | Daily FT

Heritance Hotels and Resorts has secured four distinguished titles at the World Travel Awards 2026, with three national awards recognising its Sri Lankan properties and an international title for Heritance Aarah in the Maldives.

The three Sri Lankan titles recognise Heritance Tea Factory as Sri Lanka’s Leading Heritage Hotel 2026, Heritance Ahungalla as Sri Lanka’s Leading Luxury Hotel 2026, and Heritance Kandalama as Sri Lanka’s Leading Wedding Hotel 2026. Heritance Aarah was named the Indian Ocean’s Leading All-Inclusive Resort 2026.

Internationally recognised within the global travel and tourism industry, the World Travel Awards celebrate excellence across hotels, resorts, and destinations. Recognition at this level affirms the quality, distinctiveness, and consistency of the experiences delivered by Heritance Hotels and Resorts.

Aitken Spence Hotels Chairperson Stasshani Jayawardena said: “Recognition at the World Travel Awards is a meaningful affirmation of the standards we strive to uphold across Heritance Hotels and Resorts. These awards are particularly significant as they acknowledge distinct strengths across our portfolio, from the heritage and sense of place at Heritance Tea Factory and the refined luxury of Heritance Ahungalla to the destination wedding experience at Heritance Kandalama, and the premium all-inclusive experience at Heritance Aarah. They reflect the dedication of our teams and our continued commitment to creating experiences that showcase the best of Heritance hospitality to guests from around the world.”

Named Sri Lanka’s Leading Heritage Hotel 2026, Heritance Tea Factory offers an experience deeply rooted in the history of Sri Lanka’s tea industry. Set more than 2,000 metres above sea level amid the misty mountains and tea estates of Kandapola, the hotel occupies a restored 19th-century tea factory and retains many elements of its industrial past.

Heritance Tea Factory offers a distinctive way to experience the landscapes, culture, and enduring heritage of Sri Lanka’s central highlands. Guests can discover the story of Ceylon tea through tea-plucking, tea-tasting, and a visit to the Mini Tea Factory, while nature walks, cycling, and sections of the Pekoe Trail provide opportunities to explore the picturesque highlands. The region’s heritage is also reflected at TCK 6685, a restaurant housed within a restored railway carriage at the hotel. Here, the essence of the region is conveyed through the surrounding landscape and activities as much as through the architecture itself.

Heritance Kandalama, named Sri Lanka’s Leading Wedding Hotel 2026, brings together striking architecture, integrated into the natural surroundings to create a unique destination wedding experience.

Designed by renowned architect Geoffrey Bawa and set within Sri Lanka’s Cultural Triangle, the hotel sits in harmony with its natural surroundings, with the forest landscape and Kandalama Lake forming an intrinsic part of the experience. Weddings range from intimate outdoor celebrations to larger receptions, supported by personalised coordination, refined dining, and atmospheric accommodation.

The experience extends beyond the celebration, with couples and their guests able to explore the region’s cultural and natural heritage, including Sigiriya and Dambulla, as well as enjoy nature experiences, wildlife excursions, and the hotel’s own immersive offerings. Signature dining experiences, including the Bawa Cave Dinner and village-inspired dining, further showcase the destination’s distinct culinary and cultural character.

Heritance Ahungalla was recognised as Sri Lanka’s Leading Luxury Hotel 2026, adding a significant accolade to the portfolio’s coastal offering. Designed by Geoffrey Bawa and located along Sri Lanka’s southern coastline, the resort combines tropical modernist architecture with ocean views, spacious accommodation, personalised service, and a range of beachside and family-friendly experiences.

In the Maldives, Heritance Aarah was named Indian Ocean’s Leading All-Inclusive Resort 2026. Located in Raa Atoll, the resort’s Premium All-Inclusive experience brings together seven restaurants and five bars, wellness at IASO Spa, marine activities, and opportunities to discover Maldivian culture. This recognition highlights the resort’s distinctive approach to combining personalised service with culinary delights, wellness, and island experiences.

Together, the four World Travel Awards titles recognise the diversity of Heritance Hotels and Resorts’ portfolio across Sri Lanka and the Maldives, celebrating Sri Lanka tea heritage in the central highlands, the architectural and natural legacy of the Cultural Triangle, and serene coastal hospitality. These hard-won accolades reflect Heritance’s commitment to creating experiences connected to each destination’s culture, landscape, and sense of place, while meeting and exceeding internationally recognised standards of hospitality.
